condition: One-time hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV screening in adults
summary: 36-year-old man at a wellness visit, never tested for blood-borne viruses, tattoos, not vaccinated against hepatitis B. USPSTF 2020 (HCV 18–79 once), CDC 2023 (HBV triple panel once), USPSTF 2019 (HIV 15–65).

inputs.hpi: Well 36-year-old man at a wellness visit before starting work on a cruise ship. Never tested for hepatitis B, hepatitis C or HIV. Several tattoos. No hepatitis B vaccination on record. No jaundice.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Health check — blood-borne virus screening
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Asymptomatic. One-time screening: HCV antibody, hepatitis B triple panel (HBsAg, anti-HBs, anti-HBc), HIV. Hepatitis B vaccination if non-immune.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Hepatitis serology is suggested only inside the jaundice/liver/hepatic-lesion prompts; there is no universal once-in-adulthood HCV, HBV or HIV screening prompt (the iOS ScreeningEngine has HCV 18–79 and HIV 15–65).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add blood-borne-virus screening prompts: HCV antibody once 18–79, HBV triple panel once ≥ 18, HIV 15–65.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: See inv-hcv: no universal HBV screening prompt.
See inv-hcv: no HIV screening prompt.

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for hepatitis C virus infection in adolescents and adults
guideline.section: Screen all adults aged 18–79 for HCV infection (grade B)
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for hepatitis C virus infection in adolescents and adults: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2020;323:970–975.

guideline.name: CDC recommendations — screening and testing for hepatitis B virus infection
guideline.section: Screen all adults ≥ 18 at least once in a lifetime using the triple panel (HBsAg, anti-HBs, total anti-HBc)
guideline.citation: Conners EE, Panagiotakopoulos L, Hofmeister MG, et al. Screening and testing for hepatitis B virus infection: CDC recommendations — United States, 2023. MMWR Recomm Rep. 2023;72(1):1–25.

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for HIV infection
guideline.section: Screen adolescents and adults aged 15–65 for HIV infection (grade A)
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for HIV infection: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2019;321:2326–2336.

rationale: Universal once-in-a-lifetime screening for HCV, HBV and HIV is recommended for adults; a surgical practice offering wellness care should prompt for it, and it matters before any operation.

authoring.author: Claude (prevention/screening, obstetric-gynaecological mimics and paediatric surgery cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Every citation is verified: false. iOS outcomes are unverified (not run on Linux); triage after the first CI run.
